## 🐛 Fixed

- The rainbow mode's active-row highlight silently collapsed to the same flat wash as every other row, in both `on` and `reactive` mode, because `.glim-tint`'s own box-shadow declaration has higher CSS specificity than a typical single-class `.active`-style app rule and always won the cascade - an adopting app's own "this one is selected" class needs to ALSO carry the shared `.glim-active` marker, not just its own app-specific equivalent, for `tokens.css`'s composition rule to engage at all. `[data-rainbow] .glim-tint.glim-active` now covers both `on` and `reactive` (the previous fix, in 1.3.0's reactive-mode work, only generalised to the mode it happened to be tested against). Found via a real adopting app (TrickWork) whose queue never carried `.glim-active` on its own active row.
- The wash opacity (7%) shipped in 1.0.0 drew three independent "the mode does nothing when I turn it on" reports from the same adopting app before anyone measured the actual rendered colour rather than eyeballing it - it was applying correctly the whole time, just under the threshold a person registers as change. Raised to 16% (the selected-row soft tint: 14% → 22%).

## ⚡ Improved

- The Accent axis gains a documented picker layout: presets, the custom colour input, and a reset badge all in **one row, all the same size** (the native colour input no longer reads as a mismatched rectangle glued on after circular swatches), reset pinned to the trailing edge as an icon badge, and every swatch in the row following the shape engine.
- The Language axis's flag-emoji-prefixed plain `<select>` is now explicitly the *default*, not a framework-gated mandate: any adopting app (framework or not) whose language field or option list still reads as cramped after reasonable padding may build a custom button+listbox dropdown instead - a native select's own field height and open-list row padding are effectively unstyleable, and a dozens-of-entries language list is exactly where that stops being cosmetic.
- Rule 13 (everything clickable is a badge) now says explicitly: a small, single-purpose action badge (copy, reset, undo) carries an icon, not a text label - the name lives in `title`/`aria-label` instead, matching how icon-only toggles already work. Primary, sentence-length actions ("Export settings") are unaffected.
